ORDER 1. With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 14.01.2019 passed in MACC No.300029/2016 by the 2nd Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mandleshwar whereby a total sum of Rs.2,86,393/- has been awarded to her by way of compensation.

entities.text: 2nd Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mandleshwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. As per the appellant, on 23.10.2015, she along with her husband was coming on a motor cycle from Gram Selda to Pithampur.

At about 1.00 p.m., near Shanti Nagar Lepa Phate respondent No.1 drove vehicle bearing registration No.MP09-HH-2554 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against her motor cycle as a result of which she fell down and suffered grievous injuries all over her body.

She was taken to the hospital for treatment where she remained NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:11489 2 MA-2102-2019 under treatment for a considerable period of time.
4. Thereafter the appellant filed an application under Section 166, 140 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.41,50,000/- to her by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 Insurance Company by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has Rekha Bai vs Satish on 1 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95512407/
1 awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.
5. This appeal for enhancement in the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that her income which has been assessed by the Tribunal is extremely low.
She was doing the work of stitching and was also running a beauty parlor, hence her income ought to have been assessed accordingly.
It is further submitted that in the accident the appellant had suffered amputation of left leg below the knee hence her permanent disability ought to have been assessed as per the schedule.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 Insurance Company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
8. Before the Claims Tribunal the appellant had categorically stated that at the time of the accident she was doing the work of stitching and was also running a beauty parlor.
She has done a diploma in that regard.
Even though no accounts of her income was adduced but from a perusal of evidence it is evident that she was working.

Thus her income ought to have been taken at least on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:11489 3 MA-2102-2019 basis of minimum wages which considering the fact that the accident took place in the year 2015 deserve to be taken at Rs.6,500/-
per month.

In the accident the appellant had suffered amputation of her left leg below the knee hence as per the applicable schedule under the Working Compensation Act her permanent disability is required to be taken at 50%.

On account of the accident the appellant would suffer for the rest of her life in her day to day working hence for loss of amenities she deserves to be awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- whereas no amount on that count has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The amount awarded to the appellant under the other heads is proper.
9. Thus for permanent disablement (future loss of income) the appellant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.6,500/- per month + Rs.2,600/- i.e. for 40% future prospect of rise in income.
The same annually would be Rs.1,09,200/-.
The permanent disability is taken at 50% and the multiplier of 16 applied is correct.

Thus under this head she would be entitled for a sum of Rs.8,73,600/-.
10.
The appellant is entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.10,58,393/- to her by way of compensation whereas the Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding her a sum of Rs.2,86,393/- only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhancement in the award of compensation in the sum of Rs.7,72,000/- which shall be paid to her along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.
11. The appeal is accordingly allowed and disposed off.
